_comment: The machine-readable half of CONVENTIONS.md — the single source both the
checker (scripts/suite-check.py) and the suites refer to.
contract_version is bumped by hand, and ONLY here:
major — a suite built against the old version can break (renamed required file,
new mandatory field, changed hook or MCP interface)
minor — new optional capability, or a new check that only warns
patch — wording, tightened error messages, no new obligation
Every bump gets a line in the history below with WHY. A bump without a reason cannot
be judged by the other person.

history.why: New optional capability: a suite may list its live-behaviour documentation under `live_docs` in dependencies.json; the core's live-doc-lint then gates the measurement state of added or changed rows in the suite's CI (operator decision 2026-10-24 after the retroactive review run: 21 of 35 desk rows merged unmeasured, three refuted later). Nothing becomes mandatory: a suite without the key is unchanged, suite-check only WARNs when the key is declared and no CI step runs the lint. Minor by the rule above (optional capability, warning check).

suite-check lints workflow push triggers (unfiltered push = ERROR; macOS runner = INFO). Strictly a blocking check would be major, but measured impact is zero: the class was closed the same day in every repo with CI (core PR #53, suites). Minor by measured impact, reason recorded here so the other person can judge it.
First machine-checkable version. Prose existed since 2026-08-03 morning (CONVENTIONS sections 6-8) but nothing enforced it: zero tags, zero CHANGELOGs, zero core declarations across four suites.

dependencies_optional_fields.live_docs: list of repo-relative paths or globs whose table rows document observed live-tool behaviour; added or changed rows there carry a measurement state in the evidence column (scripts/live-doc-lint.py --changed <base-ref>, CONVENTIONS section 9); declaring it without a CI step that runs the lint is a WARN

forbidden_in_tracked_files.absolute_home_path: /(Users|home)/<name> — a path from one machine never works on another
